original_value: Automatically writing stylized characters is an attractive yet challenging task, especially for Chinese characters with complex shapes and structures. Most current methods are restricted to generate stylized characters already present in the training set, but required to retrain the model when generating characters of new styles. In this paper, we develop a novel framework of Style-Aware Variational Auto-Encoder (SA-VAE), which disentangles the content-relevant and style-relevant components of a Chinese character feature with a novel intercross pair-wise optimization method. In this case, our method can generate Chinese characters flexibly by reading a few examples. Experiments demonstrate that our method has a powerful one-shot/few-shot generalization ability by inferring the style representation, which is the first attempt to learn to write new-style Chinese characters by observing only one or a few examples.

result.paraphrase: Automatically generating stylized characters is an appealing yet difficult task, particularly for Chinese characters with intricate shapes and structures. Most existing approaches can only produce styles already seen in the training set and must be retrained to handle new styles. Here, we propose a new Style-Aware Variational Auto-Encoder (SA-VAE) framework that separates content-related and style-related components of Chinese character features using a novel intercross pair-wise optimization method. As a result, our method can flexibly generate Chinese characters from just a few examples. Experiments show strong one-shot/few-shot generalization through style representation inference, marking the first attempt to learn new-style Chinese characters from only one or a few examples.
